distillation.note_on_file_size: Params shrink 9.4x (small vs teacher) but file size only shrinks ~1.6x, because every checkpoint bakes in the same frozen per-card MiniLM/structured embedding table regardless of model width.
distillation.note_on_latency: Distillation did not meaningfully reduce measured per-move latency at these sizes -- fixed overhead (candidate feature encoding, Python/ctypes call, card lookups) dominates the tiny MLP forward pass, not the network's own arithmetic.

distill_medium_vs_distill_small.note: significant: distill_small beats distill_medium ~59.3% of the time, CI excludes 50%

distillation.conclusion: distill_small is the real efficiency winner: 9.4x fewer parameters than the teacher, a statistical tie with the teacher in real gameplay (all CIs cross 50%), and the best real-game worst-case floor of all three network variants (51.3%) -- better than distill_medium's 40.7% despite distill_medium having higher offline validation accuracy (93.3% vs 92.2%). Offline BC accuracy against the teacher's soft-label distribution did not predict real self-play strength here.

fuzzing.standard: Week 0's full standard: 20,000 hostile observations + 150 self-play games, each policy through the real SafetyShell, native-crash containment via a spawned child process.
fuzzing.conclusion: All three network policies now proven at the same zero-crash, zero-illegal-action standard Week 0 established for the heuristic. This guarantee does not transfer automatically between policies (different code paths, different failure surfaces) -- each was verified independently.

router.safety: Zero policy/fallback exceptions, zero sanitised actions through SafetyShell across a real full game (test_week3.py::test_full_game_completes_without_incident); 48 network routes / 7 heuristic routes observed in that game, confirming both branches actually fire.
router.conclusion: Modest, honest result: the router posts the best worst-case floor of the three (51.3% vs 46.0% network-only vs 48.7% heuristic-only), and never loses on net to either constituent alone -- but neither pairwise matchup is a statistically decisive win at this sample size (both CIs cross 50%). Confidence gating is directionally beneficial and safe, not a proven strength upgrade.

deck_search.method: 10-round bounded local search (greedy hill-climbing over legal single-card swaps), screened at 25 games/candidate, confirmed at 100 games/candidate, fitness = worst-case win rate across a panel including a real Crustle (id 345) ex-counter wall deck built from the live card pool.
deck_search.conclusion: Real, honest finding, not fully fixable within this search's scope: the vulnerability is structural, not a tech deck-list problem. lucario_fighting's entire win condition is an ex/Mega-ex attacker line, and Crustle's ability blocks all damage from opponent's ex Pokemon outright -- a bounded swap search (which never touches the protected key attacker cards, by design) found a 7x improvement (2%->14%) but cannot solve a hard counter to its own core game plan. A full MAP-Elites/Double-Oracle population search, explicitly out of scope for this pass, would be needed to explore decks with a fundamentally different win condition.
